heading: INT. THE GRAND MERIDIAN HOTEL - SEVENTH FLOOR CORRIDOR - NIGHT

units.text: INT. THE GRAND MERIDIAN HOTEL - SEVENTH FLOOR CORRIDOR - NIGHT
We see a long hotel corridor with red carpet and gold wallpaper.
The lights are dim and it is very quiet.
Room numbers go from 701 down to 720 and we can tell this is an expensive hotel.
CLOSE ON the door of room 714.
It is slightly open.
DETECTIVE HAROLD WEEMS, 50s, wearing a rumpled brown suit and carrying a notepad, walks down the corridor.
He looks tired because he has been working all night.
He stops outside 714 and pushes the door gently with his finger.
Hello? Police.
units.name: WEEMS

units.text: No answer.
He steps inside and out of view.
A moment later a door SLAMS somewhere down the hall and CLAIRE BOSWORTH, 30s, in a red evening gown, bursts out of the stairwell, out of breath.
She is holding her shoes in one hand.
Weems steps back out into the corridor and sees her.
Miss Bosworth. I told you to stay in the lobby.
units.name: WEEMS

units.text: I couldn't. Not after what Ricky told me.
units.name: CLAIRE

units.text: Ricky?
units.name: WEEMS

units.text: The bellhop. He saw someone go into 714 at eleven o'clock, and it wasn't the man who checked in. It was a woman. A tall woman with a scar on her cheek, and she was carrying a case.
units.name: CLAIRE

units.text: A case. What kind of case?
units.name: WEEMS

units.text: A violin case. Or at least that's what Ricky thought, but he said it was too heavy for a violin, because she had to use both hands, and her whole arm was shaking, and then she looked straight at him and said, "I was never here," and gave him a hundred dollars.
units.name: CLAIRE

units.text: And he took it.
units.name: WEEMS

units.text: Of course he took it. He's twenty-two and he makes eleven dollars an hour.
units.name: CLAIRE

units.text: Where is Ricky now?
units.name: WEEMS

units.text: I don't know. He went to take the service elevator down to get his coat, and that was twenty minutes ago, and he hasn't answered his phone.
units.name: CLAIRE

units.text: Claire's phone BUZZES in her hand.
She looks down at it.
CLOSE ON the phone screen.
ON PHONE: dont trust the cop
ON PHONE: hes been in the room before
She looks up slowly at Weems.
What is it?
units.name: WEEMS

units.text: Nothing. It's nothing. Just my sister.
units.name: CLAIRE

units.text: May I see?
units.name: WEEMS

units.text: No.
units.name: CLAIRE

units.text: He reaches for the phone and she pulls it back.
They both freeze.
At the far end of the corridor, the service elevator DINGS.
The doors slide open.
RICKY, 22, in a bellhop uniform, stands there pale and shaking.
He holds up one hand.
There is blood on it.
Detective. You need to come with me. Please. Right now.
units.name: RICKY

units.text: What happened to your hand?
units.name: WEEMS

units.text: It's not my blood.
units.name: RICKY

units.text: Claire backs away.
Weems takes a step toward Ricky.
Claire turns and runs for the stairwell.
Miss Bosworth! Stop!
units.name: WEEMS

units.text: The stairwell door SLAMS behind her.
Weems and Ricky look at each other.
Neither moves.
She's not who she says she is.
units.name: RICKY

units.text: I know.
units.name: WEEMS

units.text: You knew?
units.name: RICKY

units.text: I've known since the lobby. But I needed to see where she'd run.
units.name: WEEMS

units.text: And now?
units.name: RICKY

units.text: Now we go after her, and you tell me everything on the way.
units.name: WEEMS

units.text: They both run toward the stairwell.
The corridor lights flicker and go out.
In the dark, one door CLICKS open.
Room 714.
A tall shadow stands in the doorway.
She is holding a violin case.
She does not move.
Her phone BUZZES.
ON PHONE: found you
